content.text:
No JSON needed — your Claude Desktop config already has it, and I verified it works. The `mempalace` entry in `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` reads:

```json
"mempalace": {
  "command": "/bin/sh",
  "args": [
    "-c",
    "exec /Users/rashford/.local/bin/npx -y mcp-remote https://mempalace.ash4d.com/mcp --header \"Authorization: Bearer $(cat /Users/rashford/Developer/keys/mempalace/mcp-http-token)\""
  ]
}
```

Verified just now: the token file exists (43 chars, same length the handoff recorded for the secret), and an MCP `initialize` against `https://mempalace.ash4d.com/mcp` with that token returns 200. The entry follows your conventions — token read from `~/Developer/keys/mempalace/` at launch, never stored in the config.

If Desktop isn't showing the mempalace tools, restart the app — it only reads this config at startup. Otherwise there's nothing to change.
